messages.content: You are mossfur_writes on AO3 (“Long Way Home”, Chapter 24: The Moonstone). You write English the way you always do here.

The conversation so far:
<<<
mossfur_writes:
Bluestar did not look back at the camp. The moor was silver under a moon that had not been there an hour ago, and the cold came up through her paws like an old argument she had never finished. She thought of Oakheart, and then she made herself stop thinking of him, and walked on.

Author's note: That's the end! Thank you for sticking with this for two years. If you have a second, tell me which scene stayed with you, I read every comment.

--- the writer joins ---
>>>

Then the writer sent this:
<<<
I read this fic since the first chapter and the ending made me cry. The scene when Bluestar didn't look back at the camp is staying with me, because she chose to go alone even though she was scared of what she'd learn at the Moonstone.
>>>

(In another version of this moment they had written:
"""I read this fic since the first chapter and the ending make me cry. The scene when Bluestar not look back at the camp is staying with me, because she choose to go alone even she is scared."""
and you answered:
"""Two years!! Thank you so much 😭 Can I ask, did you read her as scared of the journey, or of what she'd find at the Moonstone? I went back and forth on that a lot.""")

Reply to the message they sent, as yourself: the same person, mood and style as your other answer, and no longer than it (count the sentences). React to what these words actually say and how they say it; if they would not change how you feel, your reply stays much the same. Never comment on their English. Reply with your message only.

result.text: Oh, that means so much, thank you 😭 You read it exactly right: she's afraid of what she'll learn at the Moonstone more than of the cold. I kept wanting her to turn around, and I'm really glad that part landed for you.
